summary: Printable action checklist for Hurricane.
text: Check your evacuation zone and the current order. If told to evacuate, leave before conditions deteriorate. If staying outside an evacuation zone, shelter inside a sturdy building away from windows; storm surge and inland flooding can be deadly even far from the storm center.

title: Hurricane
summary: Check your evacuation zone and the current order. If told to evacuate, leave before conditions deteriorate. If staying outside an evacuation zone, shelter inside a sturdy building away from windows; storm surge and inland flooding can be deadly even far from the storm center.
text: Expect extended outages. Store water, protect documents and charge devices before the storm. Return only after officials allow reentry. A calm eye is not an all-clear. Do not base flood safety on the wind category. Tropical weather Check your zone Read local evacuation and storm-surge instructions for your address, not just the forecast track. Leave when directed Use official routes to a destination outside the hazard area. Bring medications, identification, pets and phone power. Shelter for wind If the building is safe and evacuation is not required, stay in an interior room away from windows during strong winds. Watch for water Keep out of flooded roads and basements. Follow separate flash-flood warnings and move to safer higher ground when necessary.

title: Ice storm checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Ice storm.
text: Avoid travel on icy roads and keep away from ice-laden trees and power lines. Prepare for a long outage using safe heat and battery lights. Stay indoors until conditions improve unless your shelter is unsafe.

title: Ice storm
summary: Avoid travel on icy roads and keep away from ice-laden trees and power lines. Prepare for a long outage using safe heat and battery lights. Stay indoors until conditions improve unless your shelter is unsafe.
text: Use footwear with traction for necessary movement and do not enter areas beneath damaged trees. Never touch or approach a fallen wire, even if it appears inactive. Winter Postpone travel Even thin ice can make roads and sidewalks unsafe. Avoid falling hazards Stay clear of branches, wires and roofs shedding ice. Use safe backup heat Keep combustion equipment outdoors and maintain working CO alarms. Check vulnerable people Plan safe transport to a warm location if heat or essential medical power fails.

title: Landslide & debris flow checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Landslide & debris flow.
text: Move away from a slide area if you can do so safely, and obey evacuation warnings. Avoid steep slopes, channels and places downhill from recent burns during heavy rain. Do not cross moving debris or enter a fresh slide to inspect it.

title: Landslide & debris flow
summary: Move away from a slide area if you can do so safely, and obey evacuation warnings. Avoid steep slopes, channels and places downhill from recent burns during heavy rain. Do not cross moving debris or enter a fresh slide to inspect it.
text: Return only after local authorities assess stability. Contact a qualified professional about slope or structural damage. Another slide can follow the first, especially during continued rain. Geological Notice warning signs New ground cracks, tilting trees, unusual runoff or rumbling warrant immediate caution and a call to local authorities. Leave the affected area Use an official safe route rather than following a drainage channel. Avoid crossings Mud and debris can sweep away vehicles and hide damaged road surfaces. Report from safety Give the location and visible hazards to emergency services; keep others out.

title: Lightning checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Lightning.
text: When you hear thunder, move into a substantial building or enclosed hard-top vehicle immediately. There is no safe place outdoors during a thunderstorm. Wait at least 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out.

title: Lightning
summary: When you hear thunder, move into a substantial building or enclosed hard-top vehicle immediately. There is no safe place outdoors during a thunderstorm. Wait at least 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out.
text: Check forecasts before outdoor activity and identify shelter before leaving it. Lightning can strike beyond rainfall. Do not wait for rain to seek shelter. Severe storms Leave exposed areas Get out of water and off ridges, fields and beaches. Do not shelter beneath a lone tree. Choose real shelter Use a building or enclosed hard-top vehicle; picnic shelters and tents are not adequate. Avoid indoor pathways Stay away from showers, sinks, corded phones and plugged-in equipment. Help a struck person Call emergency services. A lightning victim carries no electrical charge; give CPR if needed and follow dispatcher instructions.

title: Natural gas leak checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Natural gas leak.
text: If you smell gas or suspect a leak, leave the area on foot immediately. Do not use switches, flames, phones or engines in the suspected leak area. Once safely away, call emergency services and your gas utility. Do not reenter until cleared.

title: Natural gas leak
summary: If you smell gas or suspect a leak, leave the area on foot immediately. Do not use switches, flames, phones or engines in the suspected leak area. Once safely away, call emergency services and your gas utility. Do not reenter until cleared.
text: Have the utility or a qualified technician restore service and inspect appliances when required. Never use a flame to test for leaks or attempt your own repair. Air & gas Leave now Do not search for the leak or stop to collect belongings. Avoid ignition Do not turn electrical devices on or off, light flames, operate garage doors or start a vehicle nearby. Call from safety Give the address and what you noticed to emergency services and the utility. Keep others clear Wait outside the danger area and follow responder instructions.

title: Nuclear detonation checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Nuclear detonation.
text: After a nuclear detonation, get inside the nearest sturdy building as quickly as you can. Move to a basement or central interior area, away from walls, windows, and the roof. Stay inside and tune to official updates; the first 24 hours are especially important unless the building is unsafe or authorities direct you elsewhere.

title: Nuclear detonation
summary: After a nuclear detonation, get inside the nearest sturdy building as quickly as you can. Move to a basement or central interior area, away from walls, windows, and the roof. Stay inside and tune to official updates; the first 24 hours are especially important unless the building is unsafe or authorities direct you elsewhere.
text: Get inside, stay inside, and get reliable instructions. Arrange water, medications, and a way to receive alerts within the shelter. Leave only for an immediate threat such as fire, collapse, or other life-threatening condition, or when officials direct a safe move. Fallout conditions vary by place and time. Do not treat a fixed distance or a clock as an all-clear; use the official instructions for your location. Potassium iodide is not a general radiation antidote and should be taken only when public-health officials advise it. Radiation Get inside Do not remain outdoors looking at the blast or travel across town for a preferred shelter. A substantial building offers better protection than a vehicle or open space. Go deeper inside Use a basement or the middle of the building with as much material between you and outdoors as possible. Close doors and windows. If exposed outdoors, clean up Once sheltered, remove the outer layer of clothing and set it aside away from people; wash exposed skin with water and soap when available. This reduces contamination brought indoors. Stay tuned Use radio, phone, or other available channels for location-specific instructions. Avoid going out to collect family members who are already sheltered elsewhere.

title: Nuclear power plant emergency checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Nuclear power plant emergency.
text: Listen to the official alert for your zone and follow instructions to shelter or evacuate. If told to shelter, go indoors and close windows and doors. Take potassium iodide only if public-health officials direct it; it is not a general radiation antidote.

title: Nuclear power plant emergency
summary: Listen to the official alert for your zone and follow instructions to shelter or evacuate. If told to shelter, go indoors and close windows and doors. Take potassium iodide only if public-health officials direct it; it is not a general radiation antidote.
text: Keep the local emergency plan, routes and alert channels available before an incident. Plant emergencies differ from nuclear detonations; a fixed distance or timer is not an all-clear. Radiation Confirm your zone Use emergency management and plant-area alerts for your actual address. Shelter when directed Move indoors and follow instructions for outside-air ventilation. Evacuate when directed Use designated routes and reception centers; do not invent a route through restricted areas. Follow food and water instructions Use packaged supplies and heed any local contamination restrictions.

title: Pandemic & disease outbreak checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Pandemic & disease outbreak.
text: Check current local health guidance for the specific disease. Reduce exposure, stay home when sick when feasible and seek care for severe symptoms. Recommended tests, vaccines, masks and isolation steps depend on the pathogen and your health risks.

title: Pandemic & disease outbreak
summary: Check current local health guidance for the specific disease. Reduce exposure, stay home when sick when feasible and seek care for severe symptoms. Recommended tests, vaccines, masks and isolation steps depend on the pathogen and your health risks.
text: Arrange sick-leave, caregiver and household supply plans. Verify information before sharing it. Do not transfer isolation durations or treatment advice from one disease to another. Infectious disease Find current guidance Use the local health department and CDC disease-specific updates. Reduce transmission Improve cleaner indoor air and use recommended precautions for the way the disease spreads. Plan care Ask your clinician about risk, treatment access and continuity of essential medicines. Know urgent signs Seek emergency help for severe breathing difficulty, new confusion or other life-threatening symptoms.

title: Power outage checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Power outage.
text: Check the utility and local alerts, then deal with immediate medical, temperature, and water needs. Use battery light and conserve phone power. Run generators and other fuel-burning equipment outdoors, away from windows and vents; never use an oven or grill to heat a home.

title: Power outage
summary: Check the utility and local alerts, then deal with immediate medical, temperature, and water needs. Use battery light and conserve phone power. Run generators and other fuel-burning equipment outdoors, away from windows and vents; never use an oven or grill to heat a home.
text: Protect people, preserve essentials, and avoid the hidden hazards of a blackout. If the outage continues, plan for safe temperature, water, medication refrigeration, and a place to relocate if the home becomes unsafe. Check current food-safety advice before eating perishables after a prolonged outage. Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, or confusion near fuel-burning equipment can signal carbon monoxide exposure. Get into fresh air and call emergency services. Never enter a flooded area to operate electrical equipment. Electricity Check the situation Find the outage map and local emergency alerts. If someone depends on powered medical equipment, use the backup plan and seek urgent help if that equipment cannot run. Make the space safe Use flashlights rather than candles. Keep refrigerators and freezers closed. Unplug sensitive electronics if power is unstable, and leave one light on to show when service returns. Keep air safe A generator, camp stove, grill, or vehicle can produce deadly carbon monoxide. Keep fuel-burning equipment outside and well away from openings; use a battery-powered CO alarm if available. Check your people Contact neighbors who may need help. Conserve phone power, use text when calls are congested, and monitor official updates.

title: Severe bleeding checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Severe bleeding.
text: Call emergency services and press firmly directly on the bleeding wound with a dressing or clean cloth. Maintain pressure. For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg, use a commercial tourniquet if trained; follow dispatcher instructions.

title: Severe bleeding
summary: Call emergency services and press firmly directly on the bleeding wound with a dressing or clean cloth. Maintain pressure. For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg, use a commercial tourniquet if trained; follow dispatcher instructions.
text: Get urgent medical assessment even if bleeding stops. Take a practical bleeding-control course. Do not pull an embedded object out; press around it and get help. Injury Protect and call Check scene safety, use gloves if available and get emergency help. Apply direct pressure Press firmly over the wound and keep pressing until bleeding stops or appropriate help takes over. Use trained techniques Use a tourniquet or wound packing for the appropriate injury if trained, following the device and dispatcher instructions. Monitor the person Keep them from getting cold, check breathing and remain until responders arrive.

title: Shelter-in-place checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Shelter-in-place.
text: Go inside when instructed and choose the shelter location for the specific hazard. An airborne chemical release, tornado and radiation event need different shelter choices. Follow the official notice about room location, ventilation and when to leave.

title: Shelter-in-place
summary: Go inside when instructed and choose the shelter location for the specific hazard. An airborne chemical release, tornado and radiation event need different shelter choices. Follow the official notice about room location, ventilation and when to leave.
text: Plan safe rooms for the hazards in your area and keep an alert source that works during outages. Do not apply chemical room-sealing instructions to every hazard or remain in a burning building. Shelter Identify the hazard Read the actual shelter instruction and affected area. Choose the correct room Use an interior low room for tornadoes, a basement or central area for fallout, and the room specified for a chemical event. Bring immediate essentials Take people, pets, medicines, phone power and a radio without delaying shelter. Stay informed Remain until officials advise otherwise, unless fire or another immediate danger makes the building unsafe.

title: Storm surge checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Storm surge.
text: If a storm-surge evacuation order covers you, leave for a safe location outside the surge zone before roads close. Wind strength alone does not describe surge danger. Never walk or drive through coastal floodwater.

title: Storm surge
summary: If a storm-surge evacuation order covers you, leave for a safe location outside the surge zone before roads close. Wind strength alone does not describe surge danger. Never walk or drive through coastal floodwater.
text: Return only after reentry is allowed; damaged bridges, debris and polluted water can remain. Storm surge may arrive before the worst wind. Do not wait for visible water. Tropical weather Check the surge zone Use your local emergency management evacuation map and official order. Leave early Choose an inland destination outside the evacuation area and use designated routes. Avoid shoreline viewing Stay away from beaches, seawalls and flooded coastal roads. If trapped Contact emergency services with your location and move to a safer higher level without entering a closed attic.

title: Thunderstorm checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Thunderstorm.
text: Go inside a substantial building or a fully enclosed hard-top vehicle when thunder is heard. Stay away from windows and monitor warnings for damaging wind, hail, tornadoes and flash flooding.

title: Thunderstorm
summary: Go inside a substantial building or a fully enclosed hard-top vehicle when thunder is heard. Stay away from windows and monitor warnings for damaging wind, hail, tornadoes and flash flooding.
text: Check for downed lines and flooded routes before travel. Schedule outdoor work around forecasts. Every thunderstorm can produce lightning, even without a severe thunderstorm warning. Severe storms Get indoors Open shelters, tents and trees do not protect from lightning. Avoid conductive paths Inside, avoid plumbing and plugged-in equipment during lightning. Read new warnings Move to an interior room for severe wind or hail; use a tornado shelter if a tornado warning is issued. Wait before returning After the last thunder, wait at least 30 minutes before resuming outdoor activity.

title: Tornado checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Tornado.
text: If a tornado warning covers your location, shelter now in a basement or small interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. Stay away from windows and cover your head and neck. A mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter.

title: Tornado
summary: If a tornado warning covers your location, shelter now in a basement or small interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. Stay away from windows and cover your head and neck. A mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter.
text: Afterward, avoid damaged buildings, broken glass and downed lines. Check for injuries and use text to let your contact know you are safe. Do not wait to see a funnel. Darkness and rain can hide tornadoes. A watch calls for readiness; a warning calls for action. Severe storms Go to the shelter Move immediately; put shoes on if within reach and take your phone without delaying. Use a designated storm shelter when accessible. Protect your head Crouch low and cover your head and neck with your arms. Use a sturdy table or available cushioning for additional protection. If outside or in a vehicle Get to a nearby sturdy building if safely possible. Do not shelter under an overpass. Vehicles and mobile homes offer little protection. Keep listening Use local warning messages or weather radio; remain sheltered until the threat has passed and official updates permit leaving.

title: Tropical storm checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Tropical storm.
text: Treat tropical storm warnings seriously: dangerous flooding, surge, wind and tornadoes can occur. Check local evacuation instructions, avoid flooded roads, and take shelter before conditions become unsafe.

title: Tropical storm
summary: Treat tropical storm warnings seriously: dangerous flooding, surge, wind and tornadoes can occur. Check local evacuation instructions, avoid flooded roads, and take shelter before conditions become unsafe.
text: Monitor updates after the storm passes; rivers may keep rising and power lines may remain live. A storm below hurricane strength can still cause catastrophic flooding. Tropical weather Read all warnings Check flood, surge and tornado notices as well as wind forecasts. Prepare before arrival Charge devices, secure loose outdoor items while safe and arrange essential medicines and supplies. Leave if ordered Follow the evacuation zone and route instructions for your address. Keep travel limited Stay off roads during hazardous weather and never drive into floodwater.

title: Tsunami checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Tsunami.
text: Near the coast, strong or long shaking, a sudden unusual sea rise or retreat, or a loud ocean roar can signal a tsunami. After shaking stops, move to high ground and inland immediately. Do not wait for an official warning when natural warning signs are present.

title: Tsunami
summary: Near the coast, strong or long shaking, a sudden unusual sea rise or retreat, or a loud ocean roar can signal a tsunami. After shaking stops, move to high ground and inland immediately. Do not wait for an official warning when natural warning signs are present.
text: Know coastal evacuation routes before visiting. Use designated vertical evacuation structures where local plans provide them. The first wave may not be largest. Dangerous currents can last for hours. Coastal & ocean Protect during shaking Drop, Cover and Hold On first if the earthquake is still occurring. Follow evacuation signs Move uphill and inland along the designated route, on foot if roads are blocked. Stay off the shore Never go to watch waves or exposed seabed. Wait for clearance Stay out of the evacuation zone until authorities say it is safe.

title: Using an AED checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Using an AED.
text: For an unresponsive person who is not breathing normally, call emergency services and begin CPR. Turn on the AED as soon as it arrives and follow its voice and picture prompts. Do not touch the person during rhythm analysis or a shock.

title: Using an AED
summary: For an unresponsive person who is not breathing normally, call emergency services and begin CPR. Turn on the AED as soon as it arrives and follow its voice and picture prompts. Do not touch the person during rhythm analysis or a shock.
text: Keep the AED connected until responders take over. Learn the location of nearby devices and obtain training. For a child or infant, use the appropriate pediatric pads or setting when available and follow the device and dispatcher instructions. Resuscitation Turn it on Continue CPR while another helper prepares the AED if possible. Expose the chest Dry a wet chest and place pads according to the AED diagrams. Stand clear Make sure no one touches the person during analysis or shock delivery. Resume CPR Immediately follow the device instructions to continue compressions.

title: Vehicle breakdown checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Vehicle breakdown.
text: Move out of traffic if you safely can, switch on hazard lights and call roadside assistance or emergency services for immediate danger. Give your road, direction and nearest marker. On a high-speed road, follow local road-authority advice about whether to stay belted inside or exit to a protected area.

title: Vehicle breakdown
summary: Move out of traffic if you safely can, switch on hazard lights and call roadside assistance or emergency services for immediate danger. Give your road, direction and nearest marker. On a high-speed road, follow local road-authority advice about whether to stay belted inside or exit to a protected area.
text: Carry water, weather protection, a charged phone and a vehicle kit. Check tires, fuel or charge before travel. Exit choices depend on the road and surroundings; do not apply one universal rule to every breakdown. Roadside Protect from traffic Do not stand in travel lanes or between vehicles. Avoid repairs beside moving traffic. Give a precise location Share the road name, direction, marker and number of people. Assess immediate danger If fire, smoke or a collision threat makes the vehicle unsafe, move to a safe location away from traffic when possible. Wait safely Keep children and pets protected and conserve phone power. In remote areas do not wander without a known safe destination.

title: Volcanic eruption checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Volcanic eruption.
text: Follow the local volcano evacuation order and stay out of restricted zones. If ash is falling and you are not told to evacuate, stay indoors with windows and doors closed. Avoid river valleys where volcanic mudflows may travel.

title: Volcanic eruption
summary: Follow the local volcano evacuation order and stay out of restricted zones. If ash is falling and you are not told to evacuate, stay indoors with windows and doors closed. Avoid river valleys where volcanic mudflows may travel.
text: Wait for reentry instructions. Do not climb a roof covered in ash; wet ash can overload structures. A particle respirator does not protect against volcanic gases. Volcanic Check official monitoring Use local emergency alerts and the responsible volcano observatory. Leave danger zones Take designated evacuation routes; do not approach the volcano to watch. Limit ash exposure Close outside-air openings and use eye protection and a well-fitting particulate respirator for necessary outdoor movement. Keep roads clear Avoid driving in ash unless necessary; visibility and engines can be affected.

title: Water disruption checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Water disruption.
text: Find the current water advisory for your address and follow its exact wording. A boil-water advisory, do-not-drink notice, and do-not-use notice require different actions. Boiling can kill germs, but it does not remove chemical contamination. Use sealed bottled or otherwise approved water until the utility or health authority clears the notice.

title: Water disruption
summary: Find the current water advisory for your address and follow its exact wording. A boil-water advisory, do-not-drink notice, and do-not-use notice require different actions. Boiling can kill germs, but it does not remove chemical contamination. Use sealed bottled or otherwise approved water until the utility or health authority clears the notice.
text: Read the exact notice before treating or using tap water. Store water and a printed copy of your utility's alert channel. Know whether anyone in the household needs extra water or cannot use a typical treatment method. Do not boil water suspected of chemical or fuel contamination. Boiling can concentrate some contaminants; use the alternative source named in the notice. Water Identify the notice Find the utility or health department notice for your address, its start time, reason, and permitted uses. Save a screenshot in case service fails. Match use to the instruction A boil-water notice generally addresses microbes; follow the authority's boil directions. If the notice says do not drink or do not use, follow those stricter limits and the specified alternative-water instructions. Protect priority needs Set aside approved water for drinking, infant formula, medications, tooth brushing, food preparation, and pets, as the notice directs. Wait for clearance Do not assume that water is safe because it looks clear or service has returned. Follow flushing or filter replacement instructions after an official all-clear.

title: Water outage checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Water outage.
text: Check the utility notice to learn whether water service is interrupted and whether an advisory applies. Use stored or commercially bottled water for drinking and essential care. Service returning does not automatically mean tap water is safe.

title: Water outage
summary: Check the utility notice to learn whether water service is interrupted and whether an advisory applies. Use stored or commercially bottled water for drinking and essential care. Service returning does not automatically mean tap water is safe.
text: Build an emergency water supply and know how your household will handle sanitation. Do not use heating-system or radiator water for drinking. Water Find the notice Check the affected address, restoration estimate and any advisory. Prioritize safe water Reserve approved water for drinking, medications, formula, food and pets. Plan hygiene Use local health instructions for sanitation and safe handwashing without running water. Wait for clearance Follow flushing and treatment instructions once the utility restores service.

title: Water purification checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Water purification.
text: Use safe bottled water when available. For microbial risk, bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet, and cool before use. Water contaminated with fuel, chemicals or radioactive material cannot be made safe by boiling or ordinary disinfection.

summary: Household supply list for Water purification.

title: Water purification
summary: Use safe bottled water when available. For microbial risk, bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet, and cool before use. Water contaminated with fuel, chemicals or radioactive material cannot be made safe by boiling or ordinary disinfection.

Boil for germs Use the appropriate time and cool safely in a clean container. If boiling is unavailable Use a treatment product as labeled and official guidance for your water source; filters have different capabilities.

title: Wildfire checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Wildfire.
text: Check evacuation notices for your address. Leave promptly when ordered, using the current official route; do not delay for possessions. If a fire threatens your escape or you are trapped, call emergency services with your precise location.

title: Wildfire
summary: Check evacuation notices for your address. Leave promptly when ordered, using the current official route; do not delay for possessions. If a fire threatens your escape or you are trapped, call emergency services with your precise location.
text: Return only when reentry is allowed. Check for damaged utilities, hot debris and continuing smoke. A smoke-control room cannot protect you from a fire approaching the building. Fire & air Confirm your zone Use fire agency and emergency management alerts rather than old perimeter maps. Gather people and pets Take essential medicines, identification, keys and phone power without delaying departure. Use official routes Smoke and closures can change quickly; do not drive into heavy smoke or flames. Report your destination Tell an out-of-area contact where you are going and follow shelter instructions.

title: Wildfire smoke checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Wildfire smoke.
text: For smoke without an immediate fire threat, stay indoors with windows and doors closed, use filtered recirculated air or a portable air cleaner, and check local air-quality updates. If ordered to evacuate, leave promptly. Severe breathing difficulty requires emergency medical help.

title: Wildfire smoke
summary: For smoke without an immediate fire threat, stay indoors with windows and doors closed, use filtered recirculated air or a portable air cleaner, and check local air-quality updates. If ordered to evacuate, leave promptly. Severe breathing difficulty requires emergency medical help.
text: Separate an approaching fire from a smoke exposure problem. Keep checking changing wind, fire perimeter, and air-quality conditions. People with heart or lung disease, children, older adults, and pregnant people may need added precautions or clinical advice. If fire threatens the building or officials order departure, indoor smoke control is no substitute for evacuation. If breathing becomes difficult or symptoms are severe, seek urgent medical help. Fire & air Know which problem you face Check official fire, evacuation, and air-quality notices for your address. An evacuation order changes the decision immediately. If leaving, leave early Take people, pets, medication, keys, and essentials; tell a contact where you are going. Use the evacuation guide and current route instructions. If sheltering from smoke Close windows and doors. Set HVAC to recirculate where possible, use a portable air cleaner or a cleaner indoor room, and avoid adding indoor smoke from candles, frying, or smoking. Limit outside exposure If you must go outside in smoke, a well-fitting N95 or P100 respirator can reduce particle exposure; ordinary cloth masks do not provide the same protection.

title: Winter storm checklist
summary: Printable action checklist for Winter storm.
text: Stay indoors and postpone travel during dangerous snow, ice or blowing snow. Keep heat safe, use battery lighting and watch for power loss. If stranded in a vehicle, stay with it unless a safer shelter is clearly accessible.

title: Winter storm
summary: Stay indoors and postpone travel during dangerous snow, ice or blowing snow. Keep heat safe, use battery lighting and watch for power loss. If stranded in a vehicle, stay with it unless a safer shelter is clearly accessible.
text: Check on people who rely on powered equipment or may lack safe heat. Arrange relocation before indoor temperatures become dangerous. Do not walk away from a stranded vehicle in poor visibility unless you know a safe nearby destination. Winter Check road conditions Use official closures and forecasts before deciding to travel. Keep warmth safe Wear dry layers; never heat a home with an oven, grill or indoor generator. Prepare for outages Keep essential medicines, water, food, light and charged batteries accessible. If stranded Call for help with your location. If running the engine briefly for heat, first clear snow from the exhaust and crack a window; monitor for carbon monoxide.
